title: Let an agent test your web app

chapters.title: Turn acceptance criteria into browser tests
chapters.caption: The agent writes tests. The worker reruns them and checks they fail when the app filter is deliberately broken.

chapters.title: The browser runs inside the sandbox
chapters.caption: Only synthetic app source is provided to the model. No production site, credentials or customer browser session is involved.

chapters.title: Run the complete worker example
chapters.caption: The downloadable example supplies the fixture, complete prompt, worker, artifact checks and cleanup. No paid model fallback.

chapters.title: Set the contract before the agent starts
chapters.caption: Expected results come from the caller. The agent receives an app and requirements, not a prewritten test suite.

chapters.title: Prepare Chromium in the remote workspace
chapters.caption: These commands run inside the sandbox, not on your worker. Do not assume stock OpenCode includes a browser.

chapters.title: Start a tracked server, then check readiness
chapters.caption: The local health check must succeed. Detached returns a job handle, not a ready application.

chapters.title: The full prompt: browser interactions
chapters.caption: The agent must observe real rows, select Passed, restore All and capture the result in Chromium.

chapters.title: The full prompt: artifacts and guardrails
chapters.caption: The prompt names every output and forbids fabricated results. The worker still independently checks acceptance.

chapters.title: Build and execute the agentCommand
chapters.caption: The four-minute agent command runs in /workspace. Raw reasoning stays private; only reviewed evidence is published.

chapters.title: Inspect the assertion OpenCode actually wrote
chapters.caption: The recorded assertion reads browser state. The later mutation check proves it rejects the extra visible rows.

chapters.title: Independently rerun the generated tests
chapters.caption: Fresh artifacts must be created. Existing output from the agent run cannot satisfy the independent rerun.

chapters.title: Retrieve the real desktop screenshot
chapters.caption: A real 1280 x 720 Chromium screenshot, downloaded through the Harakiri SDK after the independent run.

chapters.title: Check the mobile viewport too
chapters.caption: Real 390 x 844 screenshot. The generated test reports no horizontal overflow for this fixture.

chapters.title: Break the filter and require a failing test
chapters.caption: A browser startup error is not accepted as regression detection. The broken filter must trigger an assertion failure.

chapters.title: Accept evidence, not a green agent message
chapters.caption: Original app passes. Broken filter fails. Screenshots downloaded. Model steps reported zero cost in this run.

chapters.title: Terminate both servers with the sandbox
chapters.caption: The capture independently confirms termination. Setup failures, unavailable models and failed assertions also require cleanup.

editing: Real CLI output replay; condensed SDK excerpts; real UI recordings. Waiting removed. No speed benchmark or voiceover.
